Entries without relations: Hygraph id → Tess id ---------------------- const created = new Map(); // `${query}:${id}` → { id, published, doc } const changed = []; for (const model of MODELS) { const rel = Object.keys(model.relations ?? {}) .map((f) => `${f} { ... on Node { id } }`) .join(" "); const selection = `id updatedAt publishedAt ${model.select} ${rel}`; const published = await all(model.query, selection, "PUBLISHED"); const drafts = await all(model.query, selection, "DRAFT"); const live = new Set(published.map((d) => d.id)); for (const doc of [...published, ...drafts.filter((d) => !live.has(d.id))]) { const isLive = live.has(doc.id); const { [`create${model.tess}`]: c } = await tess( `mutation($data: ${model.tess}CreateInput!) { create${model.tess}(data: $data) { id } }`, { data: toTess(model, doc) }, ); if (isLive) await tess(`mutation($id: ID!) { publish${model.tess}(id: $id) { id } }`, { id: c.id }); created.set(`${model.query}:${doc.id}`, { id: c.id, published: isLive, doc }); console.log(`${model.tess.padEnd(12)} ${doc.id}${isLive ? " (published)" : ""}`); } const draftOf = new Map(drafts.map((d) => [d.id, d])); for (const p of published) { if (draftOf.get(p.id)?.updatedAt > p.publishedAt) changed.push(`${model.query}/${p.id}`); } } // ---- 3. Relations --------------------------------------------------------------- const idOf = (target, ref) => (target === "assets" ? assets.get(ref.id) : created.get(`${target}:${ref.id}`)?.id); for (const model of MODELS.filter((m) => m.relations)) { for (const [key, { id, published, doc }] of created) { if (!key.startsWith(`${model.query}:`)) continue; const data = {}; for (const [field, target] of Object.entries(model.relations)) { const value = doc[field]; if (value == null) continue; data[model.rename?.[field] ?? field] = Array.isArray(value) ? value.map((v) => idOf(target, v)).filter(Boolean) : (idOf(target, value) ?? null); } if (Object.keys(data).length === 0) continue; await tess(`mutation($id: ID!, $data: ${model.tess}UpdateInput!) { update${model.tess}(id: $id, data: $data) { id } }`, { id, data, }); if (published) await tess(`mutation($id: ID!) { publish${model.tess}(id: $id) { id } }`, { id }); } } console.log(`\nDone: ${assets.size} assets, ${created.size} entries.`); if (changed.length) { console.log("Unpublished changes in Hygraph (copy them by hand):", changed.join(", ")); } It's also in the repository: examples/migrate/hygraph.mjs. References and assets inside components are not linked by the script. Add them in the second pass the same way if you use them.

Queries keep their structure. The differences: Hygraph Tess posts(where: { slug: $slug }) returns a list posts(where: { slug: $slug }, first: 1) { items { … } total } post(where: { slug: $slug }) posts(where: { slug: $slug }, first: 1) { items { … } }, or post(id:) content { html } (Rich Text) body (Markdown, render it with your Markdown library) coverImage { url } coverImage { url alt width height } blocks { __typename ... on Hero { title } } Same stage: DRAFT with a token Same, with a Tess token orderBy: date_DESC orderBy: [date_DESC] query Post($slug: String!) { posts(where: { slug: $slug }, first: 1) { items { ref title date tags body coverImage { url alt } category { name slug } authors { name } seo { metaTitle metaDescription } blocks { __typename ... on Hero { title subtitle } ... on Quote { text author } } } } } Use ref (not id) as a stable key in your front-end, and fetch asset urls at render time: they may be presigned URLs that expire. See Querying and Media.

Entry counts match in both CMSs (posts { total } in Tess). Published pages render the same, drafts are drafts. Webhooks and their consumers point to Tess (Webhooks). Roles: Hygraph editors become Contributors, reviewers Reviewers, admins Admins.

This guide moves a Strapi 5 project to Tess in four steps: Describe your content types and components in a Tess models file. Import the models with tess-transfer. Copy media and entries with a script that reads the Strapi REST API and writes to the Tess GraphQL API. Switch your front-end to the Tess GraphQL API. Strapi is only read, so you can rehearse the migration as often as you like. Start with a fresh Tess instance (see Quick start) and an Admin token for it.

Strapi types map closely to Tess: Strapi Tess Notes string, text TEXT Tess caps TEXT at 80 characters unless you set maxLength (null = unlimited). email TEXT With a pattern. uid TEXT With a pattern such as ^[a-z0-9-]+$. Tess does not enforce uniqueness. richtext (Markdown) MARKDOWN Tess rejects raw HTML in Markdown: convert it first, or use TEXT. blocks (rich text) JSON Keeps Strapi's block tree as is. integer, biginteger INT biginteger values arrive as strings: convert them. decimal, float FLOAT boolean BOOLEAN date / datetime / time DATE / DATETIME / TEXT json JSON enumeration ENUM Values may only use letters, digits and _: in-progress becomes IN_PROGRESS. password PASSWORD Hashes can't be copied; users set a new password. media RELATION to Asset many: true for multiple media. relation RELATION many: true for oneToMany and manyToMany. component COMPONENT repeatable: true for repeatable components. dynamiczone DYNAMIC_ZONE Also: Names: Tess field names are camelCase (coverImage), so rename snake_case attributes (cover_image). Model names are PascalCase. Single types become a content type with one entry. Draft & Publish maps to Tess stages: published entries stay published, draft-only entries stay drafts. Internationalization: Tess has no per-entry locales yet. Copy one locale per run (add &locale=fr to the Strapi requests), into one model per language or a model with a locale ENUM field. For UI strings, use Translations. Users: Strapi admins become Tess users (the users part of the models file). End users of the Users & Permissions plugin are not Tess users.

A Strapi article, src/api/article/content-types/article/schema.json: { "kind": "collectionType", "info": { "singularName": "article", "pluralName": "articles" }, "options": { "draftAndPublish": true }, "attributes": { "title": { "type": "string", "required": true }, "slug": { "type": "uid", "targetField": "title" }, "content": { "type": "richtext" }, "cover_image": { "type": "media", "multiple": false, "allowedTypes": ["images"] }, "category": { "type": "relation", "relation": "manyToOne", "target": "api::category.category" }, "seo": { "type": "component", "component": "shared.seo" }, "blocks": { "type": "dynamiczone", "components": ["shared.quote", "shared.rich-text"] } } } becomes, in models.yaml (with its Category and components): models.yaml version: 1 components: - apiId: Seo # Strapi component shared.seo fields: - { name: metaTitle, type: TEXT, maxLength: 60 } - { name: metaDescription, type: TEXT, maxLength: 160 } - apiId: Quote # shared.quote fields: - { name: title, type: TEXT } - { name: body, type: TEXT, maxLength: null } - apiId: RichText # shared.rich-text fields: - { name: body, type: MARKDOWN } contentTypes: - apiId: Category pluralApiId: categories fields: - { name: name, type: TEXT, required: true } - { name: slug, type: TEXT, required: true, pattern: "^[a-z0-9-]+$" } - apiId: Article fields: - { name: title, type: TEXT, required: true, maxLength: 200 } - { name: slug, type: TEXT, required: true, pattern: "^[a-z0-9-]+$" } - { name: body, type: MARKDOWN } # Strapi `content` (richtext) - { name: cover, type: RELATION, relationTarget: Asset } # Strapi `cover_image` (media) - { name: category, type: RELATION, relationTarget: Category } - { name: seo, type: COMPONENT, component: Seo } - { name: blocks, type: DYNAMIC_ZONE, components: [Quote, RichText] }

export TESS_URL=https://cms.example.com export TESS_TOKEN=… # Admin token tess-transfer import models.yaml --dry-run # check the plan tess-transfer import models.yaml See Import & export for the file format. :::tip Required relations The script creates entries first and links them in a second pass. Make relation fields optional during the migration, then set required: true and run tess-transfer import models.yaml --update. :::

Create a read-only API token in Strapi (Settings → API Tokens), then edit the MODELS list at the top of the script: one line per collection type, the Strapi → Tess field names, the relations and the dynamic zones. export STRAPI_URL=https://strapi.example.com STRAPI_TOKEN=… export TESS_URL=https://cms.example.com TESS_TOKEN=… node strapi.mjs The script needs Node.js 20 or later and has no dependencies. It: Uploads every file of the Strapi media library to Tess, with its alt text and size, and publishes it. Creates the entries without their relations: published entries as published (the version visitors see), draft-only entries as drafts. Links relations and media in a second pass, then republishes. Lists published entries with unpublished changes in Strapi, so editors can redo those edits in Tess. strapi.mjs #!/usr/bin/env node // Copyright © 2026 Tess Dev Team <https://tessheadless.com> // SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-Tess-Community-Enterprise // Community edition: personal use. Enterprise edition: commercial use. See LICENSE.md. // Copies media and entries from Strapi 5 to Tess (models must exist in Tess). // // STRAPI_URL=https://strapi.example.com STRAPI_TOKEN=… \ // TESS_URL=https://cms.example.com TESS_TOKEN=… \ // node strapi.mjs // // Edit MODELS below: one line per Strapi collection type, in any order. // Node.js 20+, no dependencies. Read-only on the Strapi side. const MODELS = [ // Strapi API id (plural) → Tess model; `fields`: Strapi name → Tess name (default: same). { strapi: "categories", tess: "Category", fields: { name: "name", slug: "slug" } }, { strapi: "articles", tess: "Article", fields: { title: "title", slug: "slug", content: "body", cover_image: "cover", category: "category", seo: "seo", blocks: "blocks" }, // Relations (to other models or to media), filled in a second pass. relations: { cover_image: "media", category: "categories" }, // Dynamic zones: Strapi component uid → Tess component. zones: { blocks: { "shared.quote": "Quote", "shared.rich-text": "RichText" } }, // Values that need converting, e.g. enum values ("in-progress" → IN_PROGRESS): // convert: { state: (v) => v && v.toUpperCase().replaceAll("-", "_") }, }, ]; const env = (name) => process.env[name]?.replace(/\/$/, "") || fail(`set ${name}`); const STRAPI = env("STRAPI_URL"); const TESS = env("TESS_URL"); const strapiAuth = { Authorization: `Bearer ${env("STRAPI_TOKEN")}` }; const tessAuth = { Authorization: `Bearer ${env("TESS_TOKEN")}` }; function fail(message) { console.error(message); process.exit(1); } async function strapi(path) { const res = await fetch(`${STRAPI}${path}`, { headers: strapiAuth }); if (!res.ok) fail(`Strapi ${path}: HTTP ${res.status}`); return res.json(); } async function tess(query, variables = {}) { const res = await fetch(`${TESS}/graphql`, { method: "POST", headers: { ...tessAuth, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ query, variables }), }); const body = await res.json(); if (body.errors?.length) throw new Error(body.errors.map((e) => e.message).join("; ")); return body.data; } /** Every entry of a collection, in one status (`published` or `draft`). */ async function all(collection, status) { const items = []; for (let page = 1; ; page++) { const q = `populate=*&status=${status}&pagination[page]=${page}&pagination[pageSize]=100`; const { data, meta } = await strapi(`/api/${collection}?${q}`); items.push(...data); if (page >= meta.pagination.pageCount) return items; } } // ---- 1. Media: Strapi file id → Tess asset id -------------------------------- const assets = new Map(); for (const file of await strapi("/api/upload/files")) { const url = file.url.startsWith("http") ? file.url : `${STRAPI}${file.url}`; const bytes = await (await fetch(url)).arrayBuffer(); const res = await fetch(`${TESS}/media/upload?fileName=${encodeURIComponent(file.name)}`, { method: "POST", headers: { ...tessAuth, "Content-Type": file.mime }, body: bytes, }); if (!res.ok) fail(`upload ${file.name}: HTTP ${res.status} ${await res.text()}`); const asset = await res.json(); const meta = { alt: file.alternativeText, width: file.width, height: file.height }; await tess(`mutation($id: ID!, $data: AssetUpdateInput!) { updateAsset(id: $id, data: $data) { id } }`, { id: asset.id, data: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(meta).filter(([, v]) => v != null)), }); // Published assets show in published content. await tess(`mutation($id: ID!) { publishAsset(id: $id) { id } }`, { id: asset.id }); assets.set(file.id, asset.id); console.log(`media ${file.name}`); } /** Strapi entry → Tess input, without relations. */ function toTess(model, entry) { const data = {}; for (const [from, to] of Object.entries(model.fields)) { const value = entry[from]; if (value === undefined || model.relations?.[from]) continue; const zone = model.zones?.[from]; if (model.convert?.[from]) data[to] = model.convert[from](value); else if (zone) data[to] = value?.map(({ __component, ...item }) => ({ [zone[__component]]: clean(item) })); else data[to] = clean(value); } return data; } /** Drops Strapi's internal `id` of components. */ function clean(value) { if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map(clean); if (value === null || typeof value !== "object") return value; const { id, ...rest } = value; return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(rest).map(([k, v]) => [k, clean(v)])); } // ---- 2. Entries without relations: Strapi documentId → Tess id --------------- const created = new Map(); // `${collection}:${documentId}` → { id, published, entry } const changed = []; for (const model of MODELS) { const published = await all(model.strapi, "published"); const drafts = await all(model.strapi, "draft"); const live = new Set(published.map((e) => e.documentId)); // Published entries as visitors see them; draft-only entries as drafts. for (const entry of [...published, ...drafts.filter((d) => !live.has(d.documentId))]) { const isLive = live.has(entry.documentId); const { [`create${model.tess}`]: c } = await tess( `mutation($data: ${model.tess}CreateInput!) { create${model.tess}(data: $data) { id } }`, { data: toTess(model, entry) }, ); if (isLive) await tess(`mutation($id: ID!) { publish${model.tess}(id: $id) { id } }`, { id: c.id }); created.set(`${model.strapi}:${entry.documentId}`, { id: c.id, published: isLive, entry }); console.log(`${model.tess.padEnd(12)} ${entry.documentId}${isLive ? " (published)" : ""}`); } const draftOf = new Map(drafts.map((d) => [d.documentId, d])); for (const p of published) { if (draftOf.get(p.documentId)?.updatedAt > p.publishedAt) changed.push(`${model.strapi}/${p.documentId}`); } } // ---- 3. Relations --------------------------------------------------------------- const idOf = (target, value) => target === "media" ? assets.get(value.id) : created.get(`${target}:${value.documentId}`)?.id; for (const model of MODELS.filter((m) => m.relations)) { for (const [key, { id, published, entry }] of created) { if (!key.startsWith(`${model.strapi}:`)) continue; const data = {}; for (const [from, target] of Object.entries(model.relations)) { const value = entry[from]; if (value == null) continue; data[model.fields[from] ?? from] = Array.isArray(value) ? value.map((v) => idOf(target, v)).filter(Boolean) : (idOf(target, value) ?? null); } if (Object.keys(data).length === 0) continue; await tess(`mutation($id: ID!, $data: ${model.tess}UpdateInput!) { update${model.tess}(id: $id, data: $data) { id } }`, { id, data, }); if (published) await tess(`mutation($id: ID!) { publish${model.tess}(id: $id) { id } }`, { id }); } } console.log(`\nDone: ${assets.size} files, ${created.size} entries.`); if (changed.length) { console.log("Unpublished changes in Strapi (copy them by hand):", changed.join(", ")); } It's also in the repository: examples/migrate/strapi.mjs. Relations and media inside components are not linked by the script. Add them in the second pass the same way if you use them.

Strapi REST calls become GraphQL queries: // Strapi 5 const res = await fetch(`${STRAPI}/api/articles?filters[slug][$eq]=${slug}&populate=*`); const article = (await res.json()).data[0]; // Tess const res = await fetch(`${TESS}/graphql`, { method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ query: `query($slug: String!) { articles(where: { slug: $slug }, first: 1) { items { title body cover { url alt } category { name } seo { metaTitle metaDescription } blocks { __typename ... on Quote { title body } ... on RichText { body } } } } }`, variables: { slug }, }), }); const article = (await res.json()).data.articles.items[0]; Use ref (not id) as a stable key in your front-end, and fetch cover.url at render time: it may be a presigned URL that expires. See Querying and Media.

Moving the content of a WordPress site to Tess is easy. Moving a real-world WordPress site rarely is, because of its plugins. This page explains why, how to plan around it, and then migrates a site without plugins, step by step, with a script.

A WordPress site is WordPress plus the plugins and theme installed on it. Most of what makes a site unique lives in those plugins, and each one stores its data in its own way: Data hidden in postmeta and custom tables. Advanced Custom Fields, Meta Box, Pods, Yoast SEO, Rank Math and most others save their values as serialized PHP arrays in wp_postmeta, or in tables of their own. None of it shows in the REST API unless the plugin (or your code) exposes it, and each plugin uses its own format. Content that only makes sense with the plugin running. Page builders (Elementor, Divi, WPBakery, Beaver Builder) store layouts as shortcodes or JSON. Without the plugin, a post is either a wall of [vc_row][vc_column]… or HTML full of layout markup, not content. Shortcodes from any plugin ([gallery], [contact-form-7 id="12"], [product id="3"]) turn into plain text the moment the plugin is gone. Features, not content. WooCommerce (products, orders, customers, payments), forms (Contact Form 7, Gravity Forms), memberships, comments, search or caching plugins provide behavior. A headless CMS stores content. These features need another service, or code in your front-end, or a Tess plugin. Multilingual plugins (WPML, Polylang) link translations through their own tables and conventions. Theme-dependent content. Menus, widgets, Customizer settings and block patterns belong to the theme and its PHP templates. This is why no generic tool can migrate an arbitrary WordPress site: every plugin needs a decision, and often custom code.

Inventory the active plugins (wp plugin list --status=active with WP-CLI) and the theme features you use. Classify each one: Kind Examples In Tess Content model ACF, Custom Post Type UI, Pods, Meta Box Content types, fields, components: model them, then export the data SEO data Yoast, Rank Math A Seo component on your models Layout / page builder Elementor, Divi, WPBakery Rebuild pages with dynamic zones Behavior WooCommerce, forms, memberships, comments A dedicated service, your front-end, or a Tess plugin Multilingual WPML, Polylang One model per language, or a locale field Operations caching, security, backups Not needed: handled by Tess and your hosting Expose the content-model data in the REST API, if it isn't already there (ACF: "Show in REST API" per field group; custom post types: show_in_rest). The script below can then read it like core fields. Migrate a copy of the site first, review it with the editors, and repeat until it's right: WordPress is only read. For a site with many plugins, budget most of the effort for step 2, and for the front-end that replaces the theme.

documents.t: The rest of this page migrates a WordPress site that only uses core features: posts, pages, categories, tags, authors and the media library, with the block editor (Gutenberg) or the classic editor. WordPress Tess Post Post content type Page (with parent and order) Page content type, parent relation Category (hierarchical) / Tag Category (with parent) / Tag User who writes Author (name, slug, bio: no email, no password) Media library Assets (files with alt text and size) Featured image featuredImage relation to Asset Post content (HTML) body (MARKDOWN), converted by the script Published Published Draft, pending review, scheduled, private Draft (Tess has no scheduled or private entries) Not copied: comments (use a comment service), revisions, menus and widgets (your front-end builds navigation), and site users' accounts (create Tess users for your editors: Import & export).

In WordPress, create an Application Password for an administrator (Users → Profile → Application Passwords, WordPress 5.6+, over HTTPS). The script reads the REST API (/wp-json/wp/v2/…) with it, so drafts and raw titles are included. Then: npm install turndown@7.2.4 turndown-plugin-gfm@1.0.2 # HTML → Markdown export WP_URL=https://blog.example.com WP_USER=admin WP_APP_PASSWORD="abcd efgh ijkl mnop qrst uvwx" export TESS_URL=https://cms.example.com TESS_TOKEN=… node wordpress.mjs The script needs Node.js 20 or later. It: Uploads the media library to Tess, with alt texts and sizes, and publishes each file. Creates authors, categories, tags, posts and pages: published content stays published, everything else becomes a draft (it lists the private and scheduled ones). Converts post HTML to Markdown: paragraphs, headings, emphasis, links, lists, quotes, tables and code blocks. Images point to their copy in Tess (resized variants included). Embeds (YouTube, maps…), video and audio become links. Block comments (<!-- wp:… -->) disappear, and a literal < in the text is escaped: Tess accepts no raw HTML in Markdown. Links relations in a second pass: authors, featured images, categories, tags, parent categories and parent pages. Reports failures without stopping, and exits with an error code if there were any. wordpress.mjs #!/usr/bin/env node // Copyright © 2026 Tess Dev Team <https://tessheadless.com> // SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-Tess-Community-Enterprise // Community edition: personal use. Enterprise edition: commercial use. See LICENSE.md. // Copies a WordPress site WITHOUT plugins to Tess: media, authors, // categories, tags, posts and pages (models from wordpress-models.yaml). // // npm install # turndown, to convert HTML to Markdown // WP_URL=https://blog.example.com WP_USER=admin WP_APP_PASSWORD="abcd efgh …" \ // TESS_URL=https://cms.example.com TESS_TOKEN=… \ // node wordpress.mjs // // WP_APP_PASSWORD is an Application Password (Users → Profile), so drafts and // raw titles can be read. Node.js 20+. Read-only on the WordPress side. import TurndownService from "turndown"; import { gfm } from "turndown-plugin-gfm"; const env = (name) => process.env[name]?.replace(//$/, "") || fail(`set ${name}`); const WP = env("WP_URL"); const WP_AUTH = `Basic ${Buffer.from(`${env("WP_USER")}:${process.env.WP_APP_PASSWORD ?? fail("set WP_APP_PASSWORD")}`).toString("base64")}`; const TESS = env("TESS_URL"); const TESS_TOKEN = env("TESS_TOKEN"); function fail(message) { console.error(message); process.exit(1); } /** Every item of a WordPress REST collection (100 per page). */ async function all(endpoint, params = "") { const items = []; for (let page = 1; ; page++) { const res = await fetch(`${WP}/wp-json/wp/v2/${endpoint}?per_page=100&page=${page}${params}`, { headers: { Authorization: WP_AUTH }, }); if (!res.ok) fail(`WordPress ${endpoint}: HTTP ${res.status} ${await res.text()}`); items.push(...(await res.json())); if (page >= Number(res.headers.get("x-wp-totalpages") ?? 1)) return items; } } async function tess(query, variables = {}) { const res = await fetch(`${TESS}/graphql`, { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${TESS_TOKEN}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ query, variables }), }); const body = await res.json(); if (body.errors?.length) throw new Error(body.errors.map((e) => e.message).join("; ")); return body.data; } // ---- HTML → Markdown ------------------------------------------------------------ const turndown = new TurndownService({ headingStyle: "atx", codeBlockStyle: "fenced", bulletListMarker: "-" }); turndown.use(gfm); // tables, strikethrough turndown.remove(["script", "style", "noscript"]); // Embeds (YouTube, maps…), video and audio become links. turndown.addRule("embeds", { filter: ["iframe", "video", "audio"], replacement: (_, node) => { const src = node.getAttribute("src") || node.querySelector?.("source")?.getAttribute("src"); return src ? `

[${node.getAttribute("title") || "Embedded media"}](${src})

` : ""; }, }); // Tess refuses raw HTML in Markdown: a literal "<" in the text stays text. const escape = turndown.escape.bind(turndown); turndown.escape = (text) => escape(text).replace(/</g, "\<"); const ENTITIES = { amp: "&", lt: "<", gt: ">", quot: '"', apos: "'", nbsp: " ", hellip: "…", ndash: "–", mdash: "—" }; /** Plain text from a rendered WordPress string (term names, user names). */ const text = (html) => (html ?? "") .replace(/<[^>]*>/g, "") .replace(/&#(x?)([0-9a-f]+);/gi, (_, x, n) => String.fromCodePoint(parseInt(n, x ? 16 : 10))) .replace(/&(\w+);/g, (m, name) => ENTITIES[name] ?? m) .trim(); const slug = (s) => decodeURIComponent(s); // ---- 1. Media: WordPress id → Tess asset ---------------------------------------- const assets = new Map(); // WordPress media id → Tess asset id const urls = new Map(); // WordPress file URL (any size) → Tess file URL for (const m of await all("media", "&context=edit")) { const name = decodeURIComponent(m.source_url.split("/").pop()); const bytes = await (await fetch(m.source_url)).arrayBuffer(); const res = await fetch(`${TESS}/media/upload?fileName=${encodeURIComponent(name)}`, { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${TESS_TOKEN}`, "Content-Type": m.mime_type }, body: bytes, }); if (!res.ok) fail(`upload ${name}: HTTP ${res.status} ${await res.text()}`); const asset = await res.json(); const meta = { alt: m.alt_text || null, width: m.media_details?.width, height: m.media_details?.height }; await tess(`mutation($id: ID!, $data: AssetUpdateInput!) { updateAsset(id: $id, data: $data) { id } }`, { id: asset.id, data: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(meta).filter(([, v]) => v != null)), }); await tess(`mutation($id: ID!) { publishAsset(id: $id) { id } }`, { id: asset.id }); assets.set(m.id, asset.id); // Relative URLs (files served by Tess) become absolute for the content. const url = asset.url.startsWith("/") ? `${TESS}${asset.url}` : asset.url; for (const size of [m, ...Object.values(m.media_details?.sizes ?? {})]) urls.set(size.source_url, url); console.log(`media ${name}`); } /** Post HTML → Markdown, with images pointing to their copies in Tess. */ function markdown(html) { let md = turndown.turndown(html ?? ""); for (const [from, to] of [...urls].sort((a, b) => b[0].length - a[0].length)) md = md.replaceAll(from, to); return md; } // ---- 2. Tess is headless: your front-end renders the pages the theme used to render. Query what a post template needs: query Post($slug: String!) { posts(where: { slug: $slug }, first: 1) { items { ref title date excerpt body featuredImage { url alt width height } author { name slug } categories { name slug } tags { name slug } } } } Render body with a Markdown library, and keep your URLs: WordPress permalinks (/2026/01/my-post/, /category/news/) map to the slug fields. Add redirects for anything that changes. Starters for several frameworks are in Clients.

Counts match: posts, pages, categories, tags and media. A few long posts render the same, including images, tables and embeds. Search the Markdown for leftover shortcodes ([gallery, [caption…) and rewrite them by hand. Old permalinks redirect to the new pages. Editors have Tess accounts with the right roles.

A plugin exports one or more of these functions. Inputs and outputs are JSON strings. Export Required When manifest no at install time, to read the version and description before_write one of the two before a change is saved after_write one of the two after a change is saved
No input. Output: { "version": "1.0.0", "description": "Generates URL slugs." }

Input: { "action": "create", "contentType": "Post", "data": { "title": "Hello world" }, "actor": { "name": "Ada Example", "role": "CONTRIBUTOR" }, "config": { "anything": "the admin configured" } } action: one of create, update, delete, publish, unpublish, plus submit, approve and requestChanges on content types with the review workflow. data: the entry's normalized draft, without system fields. Return one of: Output Effect {} (or empty) no change {"data": { … }} replace the data. Honored for create, update, publish and approve, and validated again against the content type. Ignored for other actions. {"error": "message"} reject the change. The API client gets BAD_USER_INPUT with your message. If the plugin crashes, times out or returns invalid JSON, the change is rejected with PLUGIN_ERROR, unless the admin enabled fail open for that plugin, in which case the error is logged and the change goes through.

Input: { "action": "publish", "contentType": "Post", "entry": { "ref": "jb56dtysPiTvASjGtgm8Gg", "draft": { "title": "Hello world" }, "published": { "title": "Hello world" }, "createdAt": "2026-10-18T06:22:55.050Z", "updatedAt": "2026-10-18T06:22:55.050Z", "publishedAt": "2026-10-18T06:22:55.274Z", "workflowStatus": "PUBLISHED" }, "previous": { "…": "the entry before the change, or null after a create" }, "actor": { "name": "Rita Reviewer" }, "config": {} } entry is null after a delete. The output is ignored. Failures never affect the change; they're recorded as the plugin's lastError (visible in the admin) and in the logs. Entries are identified by their stable ref. Database ids are never given to plugins.

Order: enabled plugins run in alphabetical order of their names, each seeing the previous one's output. Content types: a plugin runs for the content types selected by the admin, or for all of them when none are selected. Validation: data a plugin returns must still fit the content type. Setting a field the type doesn't have fails validation, so scope plugins to types that have the fields they write.

lastError on the plugin, in the admin or with plugins { name lastError }. Server logs at warn level (plugin failure) and error level (cannot load plugin). API errors for before_write: BAD_USER_INPUT when your plugin returns {"error": …}, PLUGIN_ERROR when it fails.

Symptom Cause and fix Install fails: "exports none of [before_write, after_write]" The function isn't exported. Check #[plugin_fn] (Rust), //go:wasmexport (Go), or module.exports and index.d.ts (JS). Install fails: "not a WebAssembly module" You uploaded the wrong file (e.g. the Rust .rlib). Use the .wasm from target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/. PLUGIN_ERROR … returned invalid JSON before_write must output a JSON object, or nothing. HTTP request to … is not allowed Add the host to allowed hosts, and check the operator didn't set TESS_PLUGIN_ALLOW_HTTP=false. Timeouts Raise timeoutMs (up to the operator maximum), or move slow work to after_write. BAD_USER_INPUT: unknown field … after your plugin ran The plugin set a field the content type doesn't have. Scope it to the right content types. Changes don't apply Is the plugin enabled, and is the content type in its scope? Other instances apply changes within TESS_SCHEMA_REFRESH_SECS.

Start a throwaway server: scripts/dev-server.sh (in-memory, port 8080). Upload and enable your module with curl, as in Managing plugins. Trigger it with GraphQL mutations, and read plugins { lastError }. To test a module without a server, call it with a sample input. For example, with the Extism CLI: extism call slugify_plugin.wasm before_write --wasi \ --input '{"action":"create","contentType":"Post","data":{"title":"Hello"},"config":{}}' For automated tests in Rust, crates/plugins/tests/wasm.rs shows how to load a module through the plugin manager against an in-memory store.
Return a version from manifest, and bump it with each release; the admin shows it. Replacing a module keeps its settings, so make new config keys optional.
Plugins are managed by Admins and Owners, in Admin → Plugins or through the API.

Plugin names are 2 to 48 characters: lowercase letters, digits and -, starting with a letter. curl -s -X POST https://cms.example.com/api/plugins/slugify \ -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -H 'content-type: application/wasm' \ --data-binary @slugify_plugin.wasm The response (201) is the plugin as JSON. Small modules can also be sent through GraphQL: mutation($wasm: String!) { installPlugin(name: "slugify", wasmBase64: $wasm) { name version exports enabled } } At install time, Tess checks the module: it must be WebAssembly; it must export before_write and/or after_write; its manifest, if exported, is read for the version and description. A new plugin is installed disabled. Uploading a module under an existing name replaces the module and keeps its settings.

mutation { updatePlugin(name: "slugify", input: { enabled: true contentTypes: ["Post", "Page"] # empty list = all content types config: { forbiddenWords: ["casino"] } allowedHosts: [] # e.g. ["hooks.example.com", "*.example.com"] timeoutMs: 1000 memoryMaxPages: 256 failOpen: false }) { enabled loaded lastError } } Omitted fields are unchanged. Limits are bounded by the operator's maxima, which pluginLimits { maxModuleBytes maxTimeoutMs maxMemoryPages allowHttp } returns.

{ plugins { name version description enabled loaded lastError exports contentTypes allowedHosts config timeoutMs memoryMaxPages failOpen sha256 size installedAt updatedAt } } loaded: the plugin is running on the instance that answered. lastError: the last failure seen on that instance. mutation { uninstallPlugin(name: "slugify") } Uninstalling removes the settings and deletes the module from the media store.

Plugins add your own logic to Tess without rebuilding or redeploying it. A plugin is a WebAssembly module built with an Extism PDK, in Rust, Go, JavaScript and other languages. An admin uploads it, enables it, scopes it and configures it at runtime.

Hook Runs Can before_write before a change is saved transform the data (fill a slug, normalize text, compute a field), or reject the change with a message after_write after a change is saved react: send a webhook, notify a chat, trigger a static-site rebuild Examples in the repository (examples/plugins/): rust-slugify: fills slug from title, rejects forbidden words. See the Rust tutorial. rust-webhook: POSTs a notification when entries are published. go-reading-time: computes a reading time. See the Go tutorial. js-moderation: trims text, checks required fields before publishing. See the JavaScript tutorial.

Sandboxed: no filesystem, no environment, no network unless allowed, plus a timeout and a memory cap. See Sandbox. Any language with an Extism PDK. Works everywhere Tess runs, including AWS Lambda. Hot-loaded: enable, disable or replace a plugin while Tess runs. Built-in features (search indexing, media cleanup) use the same hook system in the core.

Build a .wasm module (Rust, Go, JavaScript). Upload it in Admin → Plugins, or with the API. It is installed disabled. Configure: content types, JSON config, allowed hosts, timeout, memory, fail-open. Enable. It runs immediately on the instance that handled the change, and on the others within TESS_SCHEMA_REFRESH_SECS. Read the contract before writing your first plugin. :::info Official plugins The Enterprise edition includes plugins maintained by the Tess Dev Team. They're installed and managed exactly like your own. :::

Plugins run inside a WebAssembly sandbox (Extism on Wasmtime, WASI enabled): Default per plugin Operator maximum Filesystem, environment variables none n/a Outgoing HTTP none only to the plugin's allowed hosts; never if TESS_PLUGIN_ALLOW_HTTP=false Timeout 1000 ms TESS_PLUGIN_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS (10 000) Memory 256 pages (16 MiB) TESS_PLUGIN_MAX_MEMORY_PAGES (1024 = 64 MiB) Module size n/a TESS_PLUGIN_MAX_MODULE_BYTES (20 MiB) Allowed hosts are host names such as hooks.example.com, optionally with a port, and wildcards like *.example.com. URLs and schemes are rejected. Integrity: modules are stored in the media store under plugins/. Their SHA-256 checksum is recorded at install time and verified at every load. Configuration is plain JSON given to every call. Don't put secrets you can't afford to show to other Admins there.

Plugins run inside the request that triggered them: a slow before_write slows down every save. Keep before_write fast and local, and do slow work (HTTP calls) in after_write, ideally delegating to a webhook receiver. Each plugin instance processes one call at a time.

Only Admins and Owners can install plugins, and they're installed disabled. Before enabling one: read its source or trust its publisher; check which hosts it asks you to allow; scope it to the content types it needs; keep fail open off for validation plugins, so a broken plugin blocks writes rather than letting invalid data through.

Go 1.24 and later can export functions to WebAssembly with //go:wasmexport. This plugin (examples/plugins/go-reading-time, built and tested by the project's test suite) stores the reading time of a text field into an INT field.
mkdir reading-time && cd reading-time go mod init example.com/tess-plugins/reading-time go get github.com/extism/go-pdk

main.go: // Example CMS plugin in Go: stores an estimated reading time (minutes) of a // text field into an Int field whenever an entry is created or updated. // // Config: {"sourceField": "body", "targetField": "readingTime", "wordsPerMinute": 200} // // Build (Go >= 1.24): // // GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm go build -buildmode=c-shared -o reading-time.wasm . package main import ( "math" "strings" "github.com/extism/go-pdk" ) type input struct { Action string `json:"action"` ContentType string `json:"contentType"` Data map[string]any `json:"data"` Config struct { SourceField string `json:"sourceField"` TargetField string `json:"targetField"` WordsPerMinute float64 `json:"wordsPerMinute"` } `json:"config"` } //go:wasmexport manifest func manifest() int32 { pdk.OutputJSON(map[string]string{ "version": "1.0.0", "description": "Computes the reading time of a text field.", }) return 0 } //go:wasmexport before_write func beforeWrite() int32 { var in input if err := pdk.InputJSON(&in); err != nil { pdk.SetError(err) return 1 } if in.Action != "create" && in.Action != "update" { pdk.OutputString("{}") return 0 } src, dst, wpm := in.Config.SourceField, in.Config.TargetField, in.Config.WordsPerMinute if src == "" { src = "body" } if dst == "" { dst = "readingTime" } if wpm <= 0 { wpm = 200 } text, _ := in.Data[src].(string) words := len(strings.Fields(text)) in.Data[dst] = int(math.Ceil(float64(words) / wpm)) pdk.OutputJSON(map[string]any{"data": in.Data}) return 0 } func main() {}
GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm go build -buildmode=c-shared -o reading-time.wasm .

Add an INT field readingTime to the content types you want, and scope the plugin to them. Install and enable the plugin (see Managing plugins). Optionally configure {"sourceField": "body", "targetField": "readingTime", "wordsPerMinute": 200}. A 450-word body yields readingTime: 3. tip Go modules are larger than Rust ones (a few MB), well within the default 20 MiB module limit. TinyGo produces smaller modules if size matters.

The Extism JS PDK compiles JavaScript to WebAssembly. The example examples/plugins/js-moderation trims every string field on save, enforces a maximum title length, and refuses to publish entries whose configured fields are empty. note This example is not compiled by the project's test suite, which would need the extism-js toolchain. The Rust and Go examples are built and tested.

index.js: // Example CMS plugin in JavaScript: blocks publishing until required fields // are filled, and trims every string field on save. // // Config: {"requiredOnPublish": ["excerpt", "author"], "maxTitleLength": 120} // // Build with the Extism JS PDK (https://github.com/extism/js-pdk): // extism-js index.js -i index.d.ts -o moderation.wasm function manifest() { Host.outputString( JSON.stringify({ version: "1.0.0", description: "Trims text and checks fields before publishing." }), ); } function before_write() { const input = JSON.parse(Host.inputString()); const config = input.config || {}; const data = input.data || {}; if (input.action === "create" || input.action === "update") { for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(data)) { if (typeof value === "string") data[key] = value.trim(); } const max = config.maxTitleLength; if (max && typeof data.title === "string" && data.title.length > max) { Host.outputString(JSON.stringify({ error: `title is longer than ${max} characters` })); return; } Host.outputString(JSON.stringify({ data })); return; } if (input.action === "publish") { const missing = (config.requiredOnPublish || []).filter( (field) => data[field] === undefined || data[field] === null || data[field] === "", ); if (missing.length > 0) { Host.outputString(JSON.stringify({ error: `cannot publish, missing: ${missing.join(", ")}` })); return; } } Host.outputString("{}"); } module.exports = { manifest, before_write }; index.d.ts declares the exports for the compiler: declare module "main" { export function manifest(): I32; export function before_write(): I32; }
Install the extism-js compiler (see the PDK's README), then: extism-js index.js -i index.d.ts -o moderation.wasm

{ "requiredOnPublish": ["excerpt", "author"], "maxTitleLength": 120 } A publish with an empty excerpt is rejected with cannot publish, missing: excerpt. On content types with the review workflow, entries are published by approve rather than publish. To enforce the check there too, test input.action === "approve" as well. To catch problems before reviewers see them, also test "submit".
We'll build slugify, which fills a slug field from title and rejects forbidden words. It's the examples/plugins/rust-slugify example, which the project's test suite builds and tests.

rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown cargo new --lib slugify-plugin && cd slugify-plugin Cargo.toml: a cdylib with the Extism PDK. The empty [workspace] table keeps it independent of any surrounding workspace. [package] name = "slugify-plugin" version = "1.0.0" edition = "2024" publish = false # Standalone: not part of the CMS workspace. [workspace] [lib] crate-type = ["cdylib"] [dependencies] extism-pdk = "1" serde_json = "1" [profile.release] opt-level = "s" lto = true strip = true

src/lib.rs: //! Example CMS plugin: fills a slug field from a source field and rejects //! entries containing forbidden words. //! //! Plugin config (JSON, set in the admin "Plugins" page): //! `{"sourceField": "title", "slugField": "slug", "forbiddenWords": ["spam"]}` //! //! Build: `cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` //! Output: `target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/slugify_plugin.wasm` use extism_pdk::*; use serde_json::{Value, json}; #[plugin_fn] pub fn manifest() -> FnResult<String> { Ok(json!({ "version": env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"), "description": "Generates URL slugs and blocks forbidden words.", }) .to_string()) } fn slugify(s: &str) -> String { let mut out = String::new(); for c in s.chars().flat_map(char::to_lowercase) { let c = match c { 'à' | 'á' | 'â' | 'ä' | 'ã' => 'a', 'ç' => 'c', 'è' | 'é' | 'ê' | 'ë' => 'e', 'ì' | 'í' | 'î' | 'ï' => 'i', 'ò' | 'ó' | 'ô' | 'ö' | 'õ' => 'o', 'ù' | 'ú' | 'û' | 'ü' => 'u', c => c, }; if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() { out.push(c); } else if !out.ends_with('-') && !out.is_empty() { out.push('-'); } } out.trim_end_matches('-').to_string() } #[plugin_fn] pub fn before_write(input: String) -> FnResult<String> { let input: Value = serde_json::from_str(&input)?; let action = input["action"].as_str().unwrap_or_default(); if action != "create" && action != "update" { return Ok("{}".into()); } let config = &input["config"]; let source = config["sourceField"].as_str().unwrap_or("title"); let target = config["slugField"].as_str().unwrap_or("slug"); let mut data = input["data"].as_object().cloned().unwrap_or_default(); let text = data.get(source).and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default().to_string(); let lower = text.to_lowercase(); if let Some(words) = config["forbiddenWords"].as_array() { for w in words.iter().filter_map(Value::as_str) { if !w.is_empty() && lower.contains(&w.to_lowercase()) { return Ok(json!({ "error": format!("`{source}` contains the forbidden word `{w}`") }).to_string()); } } } let has_slug = data.get(target).and_then(Value::as_str).is_some_and(|s| !s.is_empty()); if !text.is_empty() && !has_slug { data.insert(target.to_string(), Value::String(slugify(&text))); return Ok(json!({ "data": data }).to_string()); } Ok("{}".into()) } #[plugin_fn] exports a function. The input is the JSON described in the contract, and the returned string is the output. Returning {"data": …} replaces the entry data; {"error": …} rejects the change. Only create and update are handled; other actions return {}.
cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown ls target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/slugify_plugin.wasm

examples/plugins/rust-webhook notifies a URL after changes. It only sends identifiers and metadata, never the content: //! Example CMS plugin: POSTs a JSON notification to a webhook after every //! change (e.g. to trigger a static site rebuild on publish). //! //! Config: `{"url": "https://hooks.example.com/cms", "actions": ["publish", "unpublish"]}` //! The webhook host MUST be added to the plugin's "allowed hosts" in the //! admin, otherwise the sandbox refuses the request. //! //! Build: `cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` use extism_pdk::*; use serde_json::{Value, json}; #[plugin_fn] pub fn manifest() -> FnResult<String> { Ok(json!({ "version": env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"), "description": "Sends a webhook when entries change.", }) .to_string()) } #[plugin_fn] pub fn after_write(input: String) -> FnResult<()> { let input: Value = serde_json::from_str(&input)?; let config = &input["config"]; let Some(url) = config["url"].as_str() else { return Ok(()); // not configured yet }; let action = input["action"].as_str().unwrap_or_default(); if let Some(actions) = config["actions"].as_array() && !actions.iter().any(|a| a.as_str() == Some(action)) { return Ok(()); } // Only send identifiers and metadata, not the full content. let entry = if input["entry"].is_null() { &input["previous"] } else { &input["entry"] }; let body = json!({ "event": format!("entry.{action}"), "contentType": input["contentType"], "ref": entry["ref"], "updatedAt": entry["updatedAt"], "publishedAt": entry["publishedAt"], }); let req = HttpRequest::new(url).with_method("POST").with_header("Content-Type", "application/json"); let res = http::request::<String>(&req, Some(body.to_string()))?; if res.status_code() >= 400 { return Err(Error::msg(format!("webhook answered HTTP {}", res.status_code())).into()); } Ok(()) } Configure it with {"url": "https://hooks.example.com/tess", "actions": ["publish"]} and add hooks.example.com to its allowed hosts. Otherwise the sandbox refuses the request, and the error shows up as the plugin's lastError.
